This is claimant's appeal against the judgment and award passed in M.V.C.No.861/2014 on the file of the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT VII, Vijayapura dated 18.01.2020 (for short, the 'Tribunal') claiming for enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: 2. The present appeal is posted for hearing on admission and with the consent of both the sides, the matter is taken up for final disposal.

3. For the sake of convenience, the parties herein are referred to, as per their ranking before the Tribunal.
4.

It is the case of the claimant that on 17.01.2014 at about 22.30 Hrs., claimant met with an accident, due to NC: 2023:KHC-K:5643-DB rash and negligent driving of bore-well lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-01/MH-9495 by its driver in Ramapur Village of Vijayapura District.

Due to the impact,
the claimant sustained fracture of right humerus, fracutre of left radius, head injury and other injuries.

She took treatment in Dr.Tanga Hospital, Vijayapur and spent more than Rs.2,50,000/-
towards medical expenses.

sentences.text: 5. It is the further case of the claimant that she was aged about 50 years at the time of the accident and earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, she has been suffering from permanent disabililty and unable to work and prayed to award compensation of Rs.28,50,000/-.
6. The Respondent No.2/Insurer denied contention of the claimant.

It has contended that its liability is restricted to terms and conditions of the policy insurance and holding of valid and effective driving license by driver of NC: 2023:KHC-K:5643-DB the said vehicle.
The amount of compensation claimed is excessive and prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
7. From the rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal had framed necessary issues.
8. The claimant had examined PWs-1 and 2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P13.

The respondent No.2 examined RW- 1 and got marked Exs.R1 to R8.
9.
The Tribunal, after hearing both the parties and on appreciating pleadings and evidence on record, by the impugned judgment awarded following compensation:

Conveyance charges 20,000  7. Loss of amenities and future 20,000  unhappiness  8. Future medical expenses 50,000  TOTAL 3,52,000  NC: 2023:KHC-K:5643-DB 10.
The Tribunal has assessed the age of the claimant as 55 years, applied multiplier as '11' and income as Rs.5000/- per month and disability at the rate of 15% to the whole body.
11. We have heard the arguments.
12. The learned advocate for the appellant/claimant has submitted that the Tribunal has taken income of claimant as Rs.5000/- per month, which is much lower side.
The Tribunal has also not Laxmibai W/O Chandu Rathod vs Mr. C Jayaraj And Anr on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186268312/

sentences.text: 3 considered permanent disability of claimant properly.
The Tribunal has also not appreciated the case properly and awarded meager suitable compensation and hence, prayed to enhance the amount of compensation.
13. The learned Advocate for the Insurer has supported the impugned judgment and submitted that it does not call for any interference.

14. The following point emerges for our determination:
NC: 2023:KHC-K:5643-DB "Whether the claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation?"
15. Fact of the accident is not disputed.
Similarly, petitioner has sustained injury in the said accident also not disputed.
16. The claimant has contended that her income was more than Rs.10,000/- per month.

However,
the Tribunal has taken notional income as Rs.5,000/- per month.
The accident had taken place during 2014.

While settling the dispute in the Lok-Adalath pertaining to the motor vehicle accident claim cases, notional income of the victim who met with an accident during the year 2014 is taken as Rs.7,500/- per month.
Same could be applied to the facts of the present case.
17. The Tribunal in its impugned judgment at para No.21 has considered permanent disability at 15% to the whole body.

It is the case of the claimant that she had sustained comminuted fracture of intra-artilar distal end of left radius and closed communited supra-condyla with inter- condylar fracture right humerus with head injury.
She NC: 2023:KHC-K:5643-DB appears to have taken treatment for about 15 days as an inpatient.
She underwent surgery and implants were inserted at the place of fracture.
As per the evidence of PW- 2, claimant has been suffering from permanent disability to an extent of 30 to 35% to the right upper limb and 2o to 25% to the left upper limb.
Considering all these facts, we assess the permanent disability of the claimant as 20% to the whole body, instead of 15% as awarded by the Tribunal.
18. It is not in dispute that multiplier applicable to the facts of the present case is '11'.

Therefore,
compensation for which claimant is entitled, under the head 'loss of future earning capacity due to permanent disability' is (Rs.7500X12X11X20%) = Rs.1,98,000/-.
19.

Looking to the injuries sustained by the claimant, her age and her permanent disability, so also the period of treatment taken as an inpatient, we feel that the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards pain and suffering and loss of amenities are on the lower side.
It needs to be enhanced.
On other heads, the Tribunal NC: 2023:KHC-K:5643-DB has awarded just and reasonable amount of compensation, that does not call for interference.
20. For the aforesaid discussion, the claimant is entitled for following compensation:

3. Loss of future earning 1,98,000  capacity due to permanent  disability
4 . Foor and nourishment 30,000  5. Attendant charges 20,000  6. Conveyance charges 20,000  7. Loss of amenities and future 40,000  happiness  8. Future medical expenses 50,000  TOTAL 4,91,000

Thus, the claimant is entitled for enhancement of Rs.4,91,000/-.
21.

Accordingly, we answer the above said point and pass the following:
ORDER
The appeal is partly allowed with costs.

The impugned judgment and award passed NC: 2023:KHC-K:5643-DB by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT VII, Vijayapura in M.V.C.No.861/2014 dated 18.01.2020 is modified as under:
a) The claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,91,000/- as against Rs.3,52,000/- awarded by the Tribunal and claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation of Rs.1,39,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Thirty Nine Thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the enhanced amount from the date of petition till its payment.
b) Respondent No.2 is directed to pay the said amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
c) The order of the Tribunal regarding deposit and release are not disturbed.
